newsitem.title: SPAIN: Endesa CNMV case seen weakening shares.
newsitem.headline: Endesa CNMV case seen weakening shares.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Endesa are expected to trade flat to weaker on Thursday after news that the stock market commission CNMV has filed a suit against it for failing to inform the body of plans to bid for regional utilities Sevillana and Fecsa, dealers said.

The news late Wednesday of the suit filed against chairman Feliciano Fuster and finance director Jose Luis Palomo would probably add fuel to the case for the replacement of the chairman, which has long been expected, they added.
Endesa shares closed at 8,810 pesetas yesterday, having added 1.73 percent.

"I think the only effect it's going to have is to provide an invitation for Fuster to leave. But the stock should open in line with the market, after closing flat in New York yesterday" said one analyst.
But other traders saw the stock trading up to two percent lower.

News of the possible takeover of Sevillana and Fecsa was published on October 10 in a local financial paper. But Endesa told the CNMV when it made a routine enquiry into the report that it had no plans to bid for the two companies, the CNMV said.
The commission said it was basing its case on two points of stock market law which demand that firms inform it of market moving news and must reply to enquiries.
The CNMV has the power to impose a number of sanctions, including a fine which could be up to five percent of the firm's equity.
